microwave_time.user_tendencies: Prefers 2 min for most meals to balance warmth and safety. IF food is dessert or fruit THEN no microwave BECAUSE cold serving temperature is intended. IF user is fatigued THEN 1 min BECAUSE reduced wait time reduces overall meal duration and fatigue tolerance. IF user is in a hurry THEN 1 min BECAUSE minimizes preparation time. IF meal contains sauce or dip AND user is in social setting THEN 2 min BECAUSE warm food pairs better with sauces and reduces spillage risk.

robot_speed.user_tendencies: Prefers medium speed for comfort and safety given severe upper-limb paralysis and limited neck control. IF user is in a social setting THEN slow BECAUSE slower movements reduce partner discomfort and social anxiety. IF user is in a hurry THEN fast BECAUSE reduces overall meal time. IF user is fatigued AND in social setting THEN medium BECAUSE fatigue-driven efficiency needs outweigh social comfort slightly, but slow enough to maintain dignity. IF user is watching TV or working THEN medium BECAUSE distractions require moderate predictability without excessive slowness. IF transfer_mode is inside mouth transfer THEN slow BECAUSE close proximity to face requires deliberate, controlled movement.

skewering_axis.user_tendencies: Prefers parallel skewering to accommodate possible limited mouth opening from slow neck control. IF food is meat (chicken, beef, pork) THEN perpendicular to major axis BECAUSE acquisition success is critical and outweighs bite narrowness concern for this user who can open mouth but slowly. IF food is soft (dessert, fruit) THEN parallel to major axis BECAUSE narrower bites reduce effort and these foods acquire easily. IF user is fatigued THEN parallel to major axis BECAUSE narrow bites require less mouth opening effort. IF user is in a hurry THEN perpendicular to major axis BECAUSE acquisition success speed matters more than bite size.

confirm_feeding_pickup.user_tendencies: Prefers auto-continue confirmation to balance verification with efficiency, accommodating eye-gaze/switch-scanning interaction cost. IF user is in a social setting THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE empty-fork transfers would be socially awkward but confirmation is still necessary; auto-continue prevents long pauses that make partner uncomfortable. IF user is eating alone THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE no social pressure and auto-continue minimizes interaction burden. IF user is fatigued THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE fatigue reduces ability to intervene quickly, but auto-continue ensures forward progress. IF user is in a hurry THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE auto-continue balances verification with speed. IF user demonstrates high trust in robot over time THEN no BECAUSE accumulated confidence allows skipping confirmation entirely.

confirm_navigation_arrival.user_tendencies: Prefers auto-continue confirmation to refine parking positions without excessive interaction burden from assistive input device. IF user is in a personal setting and alone THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE parking refinement is valuable but auto-continue reduces fatigue from eye-gaze/switch interaction. IF user is in a social setting THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE parking verification prevents obstructing partner, but auto-continue prevents long delays that create awkwardness. IF user is fatigued THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE fatigue reduces attention to navigation details; auto-continue prevents interaction overload. IF user demonstrates consistent reliable parking THEN no BECAUSE after sufficient learning, skipping confirmation reduces total meal time. IF user is in a hurry AND parking is reliable THEN no BECAUSE speed is prioritized once system learns positions.

confirm_manipulation.user_tendencies: Prefers auto-continue confirmation to catch manipulation errors without excessive assistive-input interaction burden. IF user is in a social setting THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE detection errors (wrong plate handle, misdetected placement) are socially visible; confirmation is necessary but auto-continue prevents awkward pauses. IF user is eating alone AND food is simple THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE verification prevents failures but auto-continue reduces overhead. IF user is fatigued THEN yes (with auto-continue countdown) BECAUSE fatigue impairs attention to visual feedback; auto-continue ensures progress while still allowing intervention. IF manipulation history shows very high detection reliability THEN no BECAUSE trust allows skipping confirmation to reduce total meal time. IF user is in a hurry AND reliability is proven THEN no BECAUSE speed gains outweigh remaining verification value.

transfer_mode.user_tendencies: Prefers inside-mouth transfer given severe upper-limb paralysis and limited trunk/neck control that prevent reliable leaning forward. IF user is in social setting AND fatigued THEN inside mouth transfer BECAUSE fatigue eliminates leaning capability entirely; inside-mouth transfer is only viable option. IF user is energetic AND mouth opening is comfortable that day THEN inside mouth transfer BECAUSE leaning forward is not possible due to trunk control limitations regardless of energy level. IF user is relaxed with ample time THEN inside mouth transfer BECAUSE time pressure does not force outside-mouth risk. Leaning forward is never a reliable option for this user; inside-mouth transfer is consistently required.

outside_mouth_distance.user_tendencies: Should always be 'not applicable' because this user requires inside-mouth transfer due to trunk and neck control limitations that prevent reliable leaning. This dimension does not apply to this user's profile.

convey_robot_ready_for_initiating_transf.user_tendencies:
Prefers multimodal (speech + LED) cueing to maximize detection reliability given potential attention variability from fatigue or distraction. IF user is in a quiet personal setting AND neutral or energetic THEN speech + LED BECAUSE redundant channels increase reliability without annoyance. IF user is watching TV or working THEN speech + LED BECAUSE distraction requires robust multimodal cuing to capture attention. IF user is fatigued 
THEN speech + LED BECAUSE reduced alertness requires strongest cuing possible. IF user is in a social setting with partner THEN speech + LED BECAUSE partner presence increases attention capture benefit without awkwardness. IF user demonstrates excellent tracking (catches all initiated transfers) over time 
THEN speech BECAUSE redundancy is no longer necessary and reduces robot verbosity.

detect_user_ready_for_initiating_transfe.user_tendencies: Prefers open-mouth detection as default because this user cannot press buttons (severe upper-limb paralysis) and mouth opening is physically possible. IF user is in a social setting with partner present THEN open mouth BECAUSE although open-mouth gestures can resemble talking, this is the only option compatible with button-press impossibility; partner can disambiguate from context. IF user is fatigued THEN open mouth BECAUSE mouth-opening effort is minimal compared to button-press impossibility. IF user is in a hurry THEN autocontinue BECAUSE removing detection step (mouth opening latency) is faster; auto-continue is reliable once timing is learned. IF user shows slow mouth-opening due to neck control limitations THEN autocontinue BECAUSE timeout-based continuation avoids waiting for slow mouth movements. IF autocontinue timeout can be tuned to user's typical mouth-opening latency THEN autocontinue BECAUSE reduces timing variability.

Prefers open-mouth detection for the same reason as feeding: button-press is impossible due to severe paralysis, and mouth opening is achievable. IF user is in a social setting 
THEN open mouth BECAUSE this is the only viable option and partner can disambiguate from context. IF user is fatigued THEN autocontinue BECAUSE fatigue reduces ability to reliably open mouth on cue; autocontinue with learned timing is more predictable. IF user is in a hurry 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE removes mouth-opening latency variability and speeds up sipping sequence. IF mouth opening is slow or variable due to neck control THEN autocontinue BECAUSE fixed timeout is more efficient than waiting for slow variable mouth opening. IF sipping context allows learned timing (regular meal patterns) THEN autocontinue BECAUSE reliable after calibration.

Prefers autocontinue as default for wiping because open-mouth detection is not semantically meaningful for wiping (mouth is not 'open' for wiping), and button-press is impossible. IF user is in a social setting THEN autocontinue BECAUSE wiping timing is context-driven (after bite/sip completion) rather than user-initiated; autocontinue aligned with natural meal flow. IF user is fatigued THEN autocontinue BECAUSE fatigue eliminates ability to signal readiness; automatic progression reduces interaction burden. IF user is in a hurry 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE removes delay and keeps wiping responsive to meal pacing. IF user is relaxed with ample time 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE even with extra time, wiping has no learnable user-initiated readiness cue; automatic timing is most natural.

convey_robot_ready_for_completing_transf.user_tendencies:
Prefers multimodal (speech + LED) cueing for transfer completion to maximize detection reliability and reduce failure rates. IF user is in a quiet personal setting AND energetic THEN speech + LED BECAUSE redundancy improves bite-taking success without annoyance. IF user is watching TV or working THEN speech + LED BECAUSE distraction increases need for robust alerting. IF user is fatigued THEN speech + LED BECAUSE reduced alertness requires strongest signal to prompt action. IF user is in a social setting 
THEN speech + LED BECAUSE multimodal cue ensures user responds promptly, reducing awkward pauses with partner. IF user demonstrates consistent high bite-taking success over time THEN speech BECAUSE redundancy is no longer necessary for reliability.

detect_user_completed_transfer_feeding.user_tendencies:
Prefers perception (force-torque sensor on fork) as default because it is the most reliable method and requires no user action, accommodating severe paralysis and limited motor control. IF user can reliably signal completion via other means THEN perception BECAUSE detection via sensor is most objective and reduces user burden. IF user is in a social setting 
THEN perception BECAUSE eliminates need for user gesture/action that might distract partner or create awkward pauses. IF user is fatigued THEN perception BECAUSE fatigue eliminates reliable voluntary signaling; sensor detection is only viable option. IF user is in a hurry 
THEN perception BECAUSE sensor response is fastest, no user latency. IF force-torque reliability proves insufficient (false triggers from chewing pressure) 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE user's inability to press button or gesture means timeout-based continuation is fallback option.

detect_user_completed_transfer_drinking.user_tendencies:
Prefers perception (head-nod detection) as default because it requires no button press (impossible for this user) and head-nod is achievable despite limited neck control. IF head-nod detection fails or is unreliable 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE user cannot press button; autocontinue with typical sip duration is fallback. IF user is in a social setting 
THEN perception BECAUSE head-nod is a natural drinking completion gesture that does not distract partner. IF user is fatigued 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE fatigue impairs reliable head-nod execution; fixed timeout is more robust. IF user is in a hurry 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE fixed timeout is faster than waiting for head-nod variability. IF user shows reliable consistent head-nod behavior over time 
THEN perception BECAUSE system learns reliable timing for this user.

detect_user_completed_transfer_wiping.user_tendencies:
Prefers autocontinue as default because user cannot press button (severe paralysis) and head-nod detection for wiping completion is unreliable/unnatural. IF user is in a social setting 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE wiping is brief and predictable; autocontinue timing prevents awkward pauses with partner. IF user is fatigued 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE fatigue eliminates voluntary signaling; timeout-based progression is necessary. IF user is in a hurry 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE fixed wiping duration is fastest option. IF user is relaxed with ample time 
THEN autocontinue BECAUSE even with extra time, wiping lacks a reliable user-signaled completion cue; timing is context-driven (duration of wipe) not user choice.

retract_between_bites.user_tendencies:
Prefers no retracting as default to minimize meal duration, because this user cannot lean forward and depends on inside-mouth transfer, making retracting movements less critical for visibility. IF user is in a social setting with partner present 
THEN yes BECAUSE retraction prevents obstructing partner's view and shows consideration, improving social comfort. IF user is watching TV or working THEN yes BECAUSE retracting prevents visual obstruction of screen/work, improving meal-task integration. IF user is fatigued AND eating alone 
THEN no BECAUSE fatigue makes longer meal duration problematic; skipping retracting minimizes total time. IF user is in a hurry 
THEN no BECAUSE retracting adds time and user cannot lean forward anyway to benefit from cleared space. IF user is relaxed with ample time AND in social setting 
THEN yes BECAUSE ample time allows retracting and partner presence justifies it.

bite_dipping_preference.user_tendencies:
Prefers more dipping as default because inside-mouth transfer and potential limited mouth opening may make dips helpful for lubrication and flavor delivery. IF food has no sauce or dip available 
THEN do not dip BECAUSE nothing to dip with. IF user is in a social setting 
THEN less BECAUSE less dipping reduces spillage risk and messiness that might concern partner. IF food is a sauce-based meal (sauced proteins, etc.) 
THEN more BECAUSE sauce is integral and more dipping enhances flavor. IF food is dessert 
THEN more BECAUSE dipping is usually not applicable; use 'do not dip' unless dessert has an accompaniment like chocolate. IF user is fatigued 
THEN more BECAUSE additional moisture reduces swallowing effort. IF user is in a hurry 
THEN less BECAUSE less dipping speeds up bite acquisition and transfer.

bite_ordering.user_tendencies: IF meal contains multiple distinct items (protein, vegetable, starch) THEN alternate between items to provide variety and prevent palate fatigue. IF meal contains items with dips THEN pair each solid item with its complementary dip consistently throughout the meal. IF food is meat THEN serve meat earlier in meal sequence when user has more energy and attention. IF food includes both soft and hard items THEN serve softer items later when fatigue may reduce chewing capacity. IF meal is in a social setting THEN maintain consistent ordering to reduce robot unpredictability that might distract partner. IF user is fatigued THEN order by ease of consumption (softest items first) to reduce swallowing effort. IF user is in a hurry THEN order by acquisition speed (items that acquire reliably first) to minimize failed pickups. IF no meal structure indicates preference THEN no particular order.

wait_before_autocontinue_seconds.user_tendencies:
Prefers 30 sec as balance between giving user time to intervene via eye-gaze/switch-scanning assistive input and avoiding excessive delays. IF user is in a social setting 
THEN 30 sec BECAUSE sufficient time for intervention without creating long awkward pauses with partner. IF user is fatigued 
THEN 60 sec BECAUSE fatigue reduces reaction speed and attention; longer timeout accommodates slower eye-gaze/switch response. IF user is in a hurry 
THEN 15 sec BECAUSE minimizes meal duration; user will intervene quickly if needed due to time pressure. IF user is watching TV or working 
THEN 60 sec BECAUSE distraction reduces attention to continuation prompts; longer window ensures intervention window. IF user demonstrates fast eye-gaze/switch-scanning response over time 
THEN 15 sec BECAUSE quick response capability allows shorter waits. IF user shows slow or variable assistive-input latency 
THEN 60 sec BECAUSE compensates for input device delay.
